source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Justify an acid-base classification from a multi-indicator evidence table.
node_labels: Matter: materials, particles, mixtures and change

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: Basic: turmeric turns reddish-brown, so the conflicting blue-litmus result can be ignored.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Cannot classify: every possible indicator must be tested before an acidic label is justified.

mx.name: surface_feature_capture
mx.teacher_note: Neutral: two of the three indicators show no colour change.

intelligence.enrichment: A classification is justified by combining all indicator observations so that the accepted label fits every row and the rejected labels conflict with at least one row. multiple_indicator_observations -> rule_in_one_nature_and_rule_out_alternatives student can copy the table rows but cannot combine red litmus, blue litmus, and turmeric into one justified label

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 7 Science question. Chapter: Acids, bases and salts. The student must decide: Justify an acid-base classification from a multi-indicator evidence table. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
